purpose: Non-destructive correction layer for Rudolf Blaschka's 1892 correspondence and related itinerary metadata. The 04 archive master remains unchanged for traceability.

policy.raw_master: 04_Blaschka_Archive_015-040_MASTER.json remains authoritative as the preserved OCR layer.
policy.corrections: Corrections are stored separately and should be applied only in research views, itinerary extraction, and public-facing prose after source-level review.
authority_order: human translation/transcription embedded in the lossless archive source
legible date/place headers in the lossless source
Rossi-Wilcox 2007 when reproducing or discussing the same letter
route/context inference, explicitly labelled as inference

record_corrections.basis: The lossless source preserves the human-translation header 'Colorado Springs 24 May 1892' immediately above the translated letter; the compact OCR captured the date incorrectly from an image/postmark layer.

metadata_corrections.corrected_value: Cambridge, Massachusetts / retrospective account of Jamaica fieldwork
metadata_corrections.basis: The correspondence sequence shows Rudolf had already returned to Cambridge by early April; the late-night Jamaica work is described retrospectively.

metadata_corrections.corrected_value: Cambridge, Massachusetts / sorting and dispatch of Jamaican materials before western journey
metadata_corrections.basis: The letter belongs to the Cambridge return phase before departure west on 12 April.

corning_2007_use.role: control text, not replacement primary source
useful_for: checking dates and place names where the compact OCR is degraded
checking botanical names quoted from the same letters
identifying which translated passages Rossi-Wilcox used
distinguishing travel chronology from retrospective description
corning_2007_use.guard: Do not silently replace archival wording with the 2007 publication's edited prose.
